summary: Shenghai Li is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2012) under Donald R. Davis Jr., alongside studies with Charles Hallisey, Gudrun Bühnemann, and traditional teachers.

Shenpen Hookham is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Reading and completed a D.Phil at the University of Oxford (~1981–1986) under Michael M. Broido, in addition to training under several traditional teachers.

Shenphen Nangwa (1871–1927) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Önpo Tenzin Norbu, taught at Dzogchen Shri Sengha in 1902, founded Dzongsar Shedra, and became its first khenpo in 1918.

Sherab Gyatso (1884–1968) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Geshe degree at Drepung Monastery (1896–1916). He founded the Buddhist Association of China, served as its president (~1953–1966), and was dean of the Buddhist Academy of China (1956).

Sherry B. Ortner is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Bryn Mawr College and the University of Chicago (~1962–1970). She held posts at Sarah Lawrence College, the University of Michigan, and the University of California, Los Angeles.
Sherry Chayat is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Vassar College (~1961–1965) and trained under traditional teacher Eido Shimano around 1967.

Shi Hu (1891–1962) was a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under John Dewey (~1915–1917) and held positions at Peking University (~1917–1948) and Academia Sinica (1958–1962).
Shi Xianda is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a BA at the University of Kelaniya and a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2016) under K. L. Dhammajoti.

Shichang Ma is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was a Buddhist archaeology researcher at the Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and joined the Archaeology Department at Peking University in 1982.
Shigeki Kaizuka (1904–1987) was a Sinology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1925–1928) and subsequently held an academic post there from approximately 1930 to 1968.

Shigeki Moro is a scholar in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and philosophy. He studied at Waseda, Toyo, and Kansai universities, and held posts at Hanazono University (2002, 2008–2015) before becoming a professor at Waseda University in 2025.
Shigemasa Fukui is a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University (~1954–1958) and later served as a professor there from approximately 1978 to 2006.

Shigemitsu Dando (1913–2012) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935) under Seiichiro Ono (~1935–1937). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1974), Keio University (~1974–1979), and the Supreme Court of Japan (~1974–1983).
Shigenori Nagatomo is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who served as a professor of religious studies at Temple University (attested 1999 and 2017).

Shigeo Kamata (1927–2001) specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology, completing master's and doctorate degrees at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo, Aichi Gakuin University (~1988–1996), and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Shigeo Yokoyama is a scholar of religious studies who studied at Kyoto University (~1973–1977). He held academic posts at Okayama University (~1983–1993) and Nara Women's University (~1993–2019).

Shigeru Gorai (1908–1993) was a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He held positions at Koyasan University, Otani University (1955–1978), and directed the Japanese Institute of Religious Folklore (~1965–1993).

Shigeru Kato (1880–1946) was a scholar in Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from approximately 1900 to 1903 and later held an academic post there (~1925–1941).

Shigeru Matsumoto (1933–2010) was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1956) and Harvard University. He later held posts at Tenri University and the University of the Sacred Heart.

Shih-Hsiang Chen (1912–1971) was a Sinology scholar who studied at Peking University (~1931–1935) and later held an academic post at the University of California, Berkeley from approximately 1945 to 1971.
